post.summary: Call the elevator to a floor
post.description: A passenger on a landing presses the up or down button. The call is queued in arrival order (FIFO); its progress is reported on the hub.
A passenger inside the car presses a floor button. The call is queued in arrival order (FIFO); its progress is reported on the hub.

get.description: The latest status the engine reported. 503 with Retry-After until the engine has reported one.

get.summary: Get the building and timing settings
Get how many people are waiting, riding and present
get.description: Staff only (ADR-0022). Counts estimated from the calls people place (ADR-0017); nobody is identified. 503 with Retry-After until the engine has reported them.
Send the token in the named header with every staff POST. Fetch a new one after signing in or out.

post.description: Sets the session cookie. Accounts with two-factor authentication send a code too; without it the answer is 401 with reason TwoFactorRequired. Five failures lock the account for 15 minutes.
Only while two-factor authentication is not enabled; each call replaces the previous key.
Checks a code from the authenticator app, enables two-factor authentication, marks this session as signed in with two factors and returns one-time recovery codes.

post.summary: Start maintenance, stop the car in an emergency, or return it to service
post.description: Admins signed in with two factors. The action is written to the audit trail before it is sent to the engine, ahead of queued calls; the result is reported on the hub as a status change. An Idempotency-Key header (a UUID) makes a retry return the first answer.

post.summary: Switch between FIFO and LOOK scheduling while the car is out of service
post.description: Admins signed in with two factors (ADR-0033). 409 while the car is in service: take it out of service first. Written to the audit trail before it is sent; the engine checks the car is still out of service, and reports the switch on the hub as a SchedulingChanged activity.
Admins signed in with two factors. Simulated passengers arrive on floor 1 and ride around (ADR-0027); they appear on the hub like everyone else. 409 when demo scenarios are disabled.

post.summary: Stop every demo scenario and remove its passengers

get.description: Newest first. Pass the page's nextBefore as before to read further back.

get.summary: Verify the audit trail's hash chain
get.description: Recomputes every link (ADR-0014). Note the head hash elsewhere: a later verification that does not reach it means entries were removed from the end.

post.summary: Arrive as a new passenger on the lowest floor
post.description: Everyone starts on floor 1. The id is random and identifies nobody; keep it to take the next steps.

get.description: As the engine last reported it. While the passenger rides, the car's floor is in the elevator status.

post.summary: Press the up or down button on the passenger's floor

post.description: Only while its door is open on the passenger's floor and it has room; otherwise the hub reports PassengerRefused.

post.summary: Choose a floor inside the car

post.description: Sent by the browser as its tab goes away (ADR-0036). The passenger leaves the building a few seconds later, unless the same passenger is heard from first, as a reloaded tab is. No body.
Only while its door is open; the passenger stays on that floor.

AntiforgeryTokenDto.description: The antiforgery token to send in the string AntiforgeryTokenDto.HeaderName header of every staff `POST`.

outcome.description: How it ended, for example `succeeded` or `failed`.

actor.description: The staff member's e-mail, when known and not anonymised.

clientPseudonym.description: The keyed pseudonym of the client address, when known and not anonymised.

anonymised.description: The personal fields were erased (a deletion request); the entry still verifies.

AuditEntryDto.description: One entry of the audit trail.

AuditPageDto.description: A page of the audit trail, newest first; pass long? AuditPageDto.NextBefore as `before` for the next page.

headHash.description: The newest entry's hash in hex; note it down elsewhere to detect a truncated tail later.

firstBrokenSequence.description: The first entry that failed, if any.

AuditVerificationDto.description: The result of checking every link of the audit chain.

carCapacity.description: The most people the car carries at once.

floors.description: One entry per floor, lowest first.

passengersDelivered.description: Rides completed (a passenger left the car on another floor) since the engine started.

averageWaitTime.description: Mean time from calling the elevator to boarding, over boardings after a call; null before the first.

BuildingOccupancyDto.description:
How many passengers are where (ADR-0026). Counts only:
passengers are anonymous by design and nothing identifies an individual (ADR-0024).

CallDto.description: A call: a hall call has a CallDirection? CallDto.Direction, a car call does not.

CarCallRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/car-calls`: a passenger inside the car chose int CarCallRequest.Floor.

DemoScenario.description: The demo scenarios an admin can start (ADR-0027). Every simulated passenger starts on the lowest floor.

ElevatorConfigurationDto.description: Building and timing settings, so a client can draw the shaft and animate at the right speed.

currentFloor.description: The floor the car is at, or travelling to while moving.

oneOf.description: Direction of the current or most recent trip; null before the first one.
Why the car is out of service, when it is.

pendingCalls.description: Calls still to be served, oldest first.

targetFloors.description: Floors still to visit, in the order they were first requested.

version.description: Increases with every change; ignore a status older than the one shown.

doorsCloseAt.description:
While the door is open: when it will close, or `null` when it stays open because the car has
nowhere to go. Always `null` while the door is closed.

speed.description:
How many times faster than normal the car runs: 1, or more while a demo fast-forwards the building (ADR-0031).
Divide the configured travel time and door countdown by it.

oneOf.description: The order the car serves its calls in right now (ADR-0033); null from an engine that does not say.

ElevatorStatusDto.description: A consistent view of the elevator at one moment. Higher long ElevatorStatusDto.Version is newer.

EnableTwoFactorRequest.description: A code from the authenticator app, proving the key from TwoFactorSetupDto was registered.

FloorOccupancyDto.description: People on one floor: int FloorOccupancyDto.Waiting for the elevator, and int FloorOccupancyDto.Present on the floor but not waiting.

HallCallRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/hall-calls`: someone on int HallCallRequest.Floor wants to go CallDirection HallCallRequest.Direction.

passengerId.description: The anonymous passenger, a random id the browser keeps.

requestId.description: Every activity this step causes carries it as Guid? ElevatorActivityDto.RequestId.

PassengerAcceptedResponse.description: Answers a passenger's step: the passenger it applies to and the id that reports its progress on the hub.

PassengerCarCallRequest.description: A passenger inside the car chooses a floor.

floor.description: The floor they are on, or the car's floor while they ride.

oneOf.description: The direction they called, while they wait on their floor for the car.

destination.description: The floor they chose inside the car, until they leave.

simulated.description: A passenger of a demo scenario rather than a person.

PassengerDto.description: Where an anonymous passenger is, as the engine last reported it (ADR-0026).

PassengerHallCallRequest.description: A passenger on a landing presses the up or down button of their floor.

PendingCallDto.description: A call waiting to be served and how many requests were merged into it.

RecoveryCodesDto.description: One-time recovery codes, shown once: each signs in without the authenticator app.

RequestAcceptedResponse.description: The request was accepted; its progress is reported through the hub's activity feed.

ScenarioAcceptedResponse.description: A scenario command passed to the engine; simulated passengers appear on the hub as they act.

SchedulingAcceptedResponse.description: The change was sent to the engine; it is reported on the hub as a `SchedulingChanged` activity.

SchedulingRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/admin/scheduling`: the order the car should serve its calls in (ADR-0033).

ServiceActionAcceptedResponse.description: A service action passed to the engine; its effect is reported on the hub as a status change.

ServiceActionRequest.description: An admin's service action: start maintenance, emergency stop or return to service (ADR-0017).

SignInRequest.description:
Signs a staff member in. Accounts with two-factor authentication also send string? SignInRequest.TwoFactorCode (from
their authenticator app) or string? SignInRequest.RecoveryCode; without one the answer is `401` with reason
SignInFailureReason.TwoFactorRequired.

StaffRole.description: What a staff account may do (ADR-0022).

email.description: The account's e-mail, which is also its user name.

twoFactorEnabled.description: The account has an authenticator app registered.

twoFactorVerified.description: This session was signed in with the second factor; every staff capability needs it.

testAccount.description:
The configured test account, signed in with its password only (ADR-0030): it has every staff capability without a
second factor, and the UI says so.

StaffSessionDto.description: The signed-in staff member, as the UI needs it.

StartScenarioRequest.description: An admin starts a demo scenario.

TwoFactorSetupDto.description: A new authenticator key, to scan as string TwoFactorSetupDto.AuthenticatorUri (a QR code) or type as string TwoFactorSetupDto.SharedKey.
